facts.statement: Aldabrachampsus lived during the Pleistocene on Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles.
facts.quote: It lived during the Pleistocene on Aldabra Atoll, Seychelles in the western Indian Ocean.

facts.statement: The species name Aldabrachampsus dilophus translates to 'Two-crested crocodile from Aldabra'.
facts.quote: The name Aldabrachampsus dilophus means "Two-crested crocodile from Aldabra".

facts.statement: Aldabrachampsus was a small crocodile reaching 2 to 2.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a small animal, reaching a length of 2-2.5 m, comparable in size to the smallest extant crocodilians.

facts.statement: The squamosal bone of Aldabrachampsus bears an outward-facing horn-like projection.
facts.quote: The squamosal bone widens towards its suture with the postorbital and the bone bears a horn-like projection that faces outwards.

facts.statement: The first remains of Aldabrachampsus were found in Quaternary deposits at Point Hodoul on Aldabra Atoll.
facts.quote: The first remains of Aldabrachampsus were found in Quaternary deposits of Point Hodoul at the eastern end of the Aldabra Atoll.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aldabrachampsus date to approximately 118,000 years ago.
facts.quote: The limestone cavities that yielded these remains also preserved the fossils of lizards, tortoises, birds and land snails and date to approximately 118,000 years ago.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from a dried pond on Grande Terre Island shows a predator-prey relationship between Aldabrachampsus and the giant tortoise Aldabrachelys gigantea.
facts.quote: Fossil discoveries made at a dried up pond on Grande Terre Island corresponding to the Late Pleistocene Aldabra Limestone show evidence of a predator-prey relationship between crocodilians and the native giant tortoise Aldabrachelys gigantea.

facts.statement: Tortoise shell fragments found at the site bear unhealed puncture wounds on the nuchal armor, plastron, and pubis.
facts.quote: Several tortoise shell fragments from the site are known to bear distinct feeding marks in the form of unhealed puncture wounds inflicted to the nuchal armor, plastron and the pubis of the tortoise.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Aldabrachampsus belongs to the family Crocodylidae.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis suggests it is part of the family Crocodylidae, composed of the subfamilies Crocodylinae and Osteolaeminae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Aldabrachampsus is a sister taxon to Voay or to Crocodylus palaeindicus.
facts.quote: In some trees, Aldabrachampsus is recovered as a sister taxon to Voay, while others find it to be a sister to Crocodylus palaeindicus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the small body size of Aldabrachampsus and Osteolaemus may have evolved independently.
facts.quote: Another hypothesis meanwhile suggests that smaller bodysize is a trait evolved by Osteolaemus and Aldabrachampsus independently of one another.

facts.statement: Aldabrachampsus lived from 0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago during the Late Pleistocene.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Late Pleistocene (0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Aldabrachampsus was described by Brochu in 2006.
Aldabrachampsus possessed five premaxillary teeth, with the second through fifth aligned in a straight line.
facts.quote: Like most other crocodilians Aldabrachampsus possessed five teeth situated in the premaxilla, however the second to fifth are all aligned in a straight line rather than following a convex path.

facts.statement: The anterior process of the frontal bone in Aldabrachampsus is slender and protrudes sharply from the main body.
facts.quote: The anterior process of the frontal bone is slender and notably protrudes from the body following a sudden sharp constriction.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Aldabrachampsus may have attacked giant tortoises head-on at watering holes to access the nuchal plate.
facts.quote: It is possible that a crocodile attacked and killed a tortoise head on as it was drinking at a watering hole, puncturing the nuchal plate at the front of the shell rather than attacking the high, better defended sides of the turtle.

rejected.statement: The horns of Aldabrachampsus are less pointed and more rounded than those of related species, with their apex located halfway along the bone.
rejected.quote: The horns are notably less pointed, showing a more rounded morphology, and their apex is located towards the halfway point of the bone.
